<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 12pt;"><b><i>Notes To Consolidated Financial Statements</i></b></p>

<hr style="margin: 3pt 0px; border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7674" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653123821" id="thunderdome-statement-801913">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588657" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em>) &nbsp; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of MBT Financial Corp. (the &ldquo;Corporation&rdquo;) and its wholly owned subsidiary, Monroe Bank &amp; Trust (the &ldquo;Bank&rdquo;). The Bank includes the accounts of its wholly owned subsidiar<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">y, MB&amp;T Financial Services, Inc. The Bank operates <em data-td-fact-id="27588658" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">fourteen</em> banking offices in Monroe County, Michigan and <em data-td-fact-id="27588659" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">six</em> banking offices in Wayne County, Michigan. The Bank&rsquo;s primary source of revenue is from providing loans to customers, who are predominantly small and middle-market businesses and middle-income individuals. The Corporation&rsquo;s sole business segment is community banking.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The accounting and reporting policies of the Bank conform to practice within the banking industry and are in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States. Preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires Management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates. Material estimates that are particularly susceptible to significant changes in the near term are the determination of the allowance for loan losses<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, the fair value of investment securities, the valuation of other real estate owned, and the deferred tax asset.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The significant accounting policies are as follows:</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">PRINCIPLES OF CONSOLIDATION</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Corporation and its subsidiary. All material intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated. <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Certain prior year amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current year presentation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">SIGNIFICANT GROUP CONCENTRATIONS OF CREDIT RISK</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Most of the Corporation&#39;s activities are with customers located within southeast Michigan. Notes <em data-td-fact-id="27588660" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588661" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">4</em> discuss the types of securities and lending that the Corporation engages in. The Corporation does <em data-td-fact-id="27588662" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> have any significant concentrations in any <em data-td-fact-id="27588663" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">one</em> industry or to any <em data-td-fact-id="27588664" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">one</em> customer.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">INVESTMENT SECURITIES</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Certificates of deposit in other financial institutions are carried at cost. All certificates of deposit in other financial institutions had balances less than or equal to <em data-td-fact-id="27588665" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$250,000</em> and, as such, were fully insured by the FDIC.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Investment securities that are <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">classified as &ldquo;held to maturity&rdquo; are stated at cost, and adjusted for accumulated amortization of premium and accretion of discount. The Bank has the intention and, in Management&rsquo;s opinion, the ability to hold these investment securities until maturity. Investment securities that are classified as &ldquo;available for sale&rdquo; are stated at estimated market value, with the related unrealized gains and losses reported as an amount, net of taxes, as a component of stockholders&rsquo; equity. The market value of securities is based on quoted market prices. For securities that do <em data-td-fact-id="27588666" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> have readily available market values, estimated market values are calculated based on the market values of comparable securities. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Purchase premiums and discounts are recognized in interest income using the interest method over the terms of the securities. Declines in the fair value of held-to-maturity and available-for-sale securities below their cost that are deemed to be other than temporary are reflected in earnings as realized losses. In estimating other-than-temporary impairment losses, management considers the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer, and the intent and ability of the Corporation to retain its investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value. Gains and losses on the sale of securities are recorded on the trade date and are determined using the specific identification method.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Management evaluates securities for other-than-temporary impairment (&ldquo;OTTI&rdquo;) on a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market conditions warrant such an evaluation. When evaluating investment securities consideration is given to the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer, whether the market decline was affected by macroeconomic conditions and whether the <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Company has the intent to sell the debt security or more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27588667" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> will be required to sell the debt security before its anticipated recovery. In analyzing an issuer&rsquo;s financial condition, the Company <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>consider whether the securities are issued by the federal government or its agencies, or U.S. Government sponsored enterprises, whether downgrades by bond rating agencies have occurred, and the results of reviews of the issuer&rsquo;s financial condition. The assessment of whether an other-than-temporary decline exists involves a high degree of subjectivity and judgment and is based on the information available to management at a point in time.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">When OTTI occurs, the amount of the OTTI recognized in earnings depends on whether an entity intends to sell the security or it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27588668" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> it will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis. If an entity intends to sell or it is more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27588669" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> it will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis, the OTTI shall be recognized in earnings equal to the entire difference between the investment<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s amortized cost basis and its fair value at the balance sheet date. The previous amortized cost basis less the OTTI recognized in earnings becomes the new amortized cost basis of the investment. If a security is determined to be other-than-temporarily impaired, but the entity does <em data-td-fact-id="27588670" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> intend to sell the security, only the credit portion of the estimated loss is recognized in earnings, with the other portion of the loss recognized in other comprehensive income.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">47</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">LOANS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank grants mortgage, commercial, and consumer loans to customers.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> Loans that management has the intent and ability to hold for the foreseeable future or until maturity or pay-off are reported at their outstanding unpaid principal balances adjusted for charge-offs, the allowance for loan losses, and any deferred fees or costs on originated loans. Interest income is accrued on the unpaid principal balance. Loan origination fees, net of certain direct origination costs, are deferred and recognized as an adjustment of the related loan yield using the interest method.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The accrual of interest on loans is discontinued at the time the loan is <em data-td-fact-id="27588671" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">90</em> days delinquent unless the credit is well secured and in the process of collection. In all cases, loans are placed on nonaccrual or charged off at an earlier date if principal or interest is considered doubtful.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">All interest accrued but <em data-td-fact-id="27588672" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> collected for loans that are placed on nonaccrual or charged off is reversed against interest income. The interest on these loans is accounted for on the cash basis or cost recovery method, until qualifying for return to accrual. Loans are returned to accrual status when all the principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and future payments are reasonably assured.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">FEDERAL HOME LOAN BANK STOCK</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank is a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">of Indianapolis (FHLBI). Members are required to own a certain amount of stock based on the level of borrowings and other factors. Stock in the FHLBI is recorded at redemption value which approximates fair value. The Company periodically evaluates the FHLBI stock for impairment based on ultimate recovery of par value. Both cash and stock dividends are reported as income.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">LOANS HELD FOR SALE</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Loans held for sale consist of fixed rate residential mortgage loans with maturities of <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588673" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">10</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27588674" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">30</em> years. Such loans are recorded at the lower of aggregate cost or estimated fair value.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">ALLOWANCE FOR LOAN LOSSES</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance for loan losses is established as losses are estimated to have occurred through a provision for loan losses charged to earnings. Loan losses are charged against the allowance when management believes the uncollectibility of a loan balance is confirmed. Subsequent recoveries, if any, are credited to the allowance.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance for loan losses is evaluated on a regular basis by management and is based upon management&#39;s periodic review of the collectibility of the loans in light of historical experience, the nature and volume of the loan portfolio, adverse situations that <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>affect the borrower&#39;s ability to repay, estimated value of any underlying collateral and prevailing economic conditions. This evaluation is inherently subjective as it requires estimates that are susceptible to significant revision as more information becomes available.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance consists of specific<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, general, and unallocated components. The specific component relates to loans that are classified as non-accrual or renegotiated. For such loans that are also classified as impaired, an allowance is established when the discounted cash flows (or collateral value or observable market price) of the impaired loan is lower than the carrying value of that loan. The general component covers non-classified loans and is based on historical loss experience, adjusted for qualitative factors. An unallocated component is maintained to cover uncertainties that could affect management&rsquo;s estimate of probably losses. The unallocated component of the allowance reflects the margin of imprecision inherent in the underlying assumptions used in the methodologies for estimating specific and general losses in the portfolio.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Corporation will be unable to collect the scheduled payments of principal or interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement. Factors considered by management in determining impairment include payment status, collateral value, and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when due. Loans that experience insignificant payment delays and payment shortfalls generally are <em data-td-fact-id="27588675" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> classified as impaired. Management determines the significance of payment delays and payment shortfalls on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration all of the circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including length of the delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower&#39;s prior payment record, and the amount of the shortfall in relation to the principal and interest owed. Impairment is measured on a loan by loan basis for commercial and construction loans by either the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#39;s effective interest rate, the loan&#39;s obtainable market price, or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Troubled debt restructuring of loans is undertaken to improve the likelihood that the loan will be repaid in full under the modified terms in accordance with a reasonable repayment schedule. All modified loans are evaluated to determine whether the loans should be reported as Troubled Debt Restructuring<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">s (TDR). A loan is a TDR when the Bank, for economic or legal reasons related to the borrower&rsquo;s financial difficulties, grants a concession to the borrower by modifying a loan. To make this determination, the Bank must determine whether (a) the borrower is experiencing financial difficulties and (b) the Bank granted the borrower a concession. This determination requires consideration of all of the facts and circumstances surrounding the modification. An overall general decline in the economy or some deterioration in a borrower&rsquo;s financial condition does <em data-td-fact-id="27588676" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> automatically mean the borrower is experiencing financial difficulties.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">48</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Large groups of homogeneous loans are collectively evaluated for impairment. Accordingly, the Corporation does <em data-td-fact-id="27588677" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> separately identify individual consumer and residential loans for impairment disclosures.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">FORECLOSED ASSETS (INCLUDES OTHER REAL ESTATE OWNED)</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Assets acquired through, or in lieu of, loan foreclosure are held for sale and are initially recorded at the lower of fair value <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">less costs to sell or the loan carrying amount at the date of the foreclosure, establishing a new cost basis. Subsequent to foreclosure, valuations are periodically performed by Management and the assets are carried at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell. Expenses from operations and changes in the valuation allowance are included in net expenses from foreclosed assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">BANK PREMISES AND EQUIPMENT</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Bank premises and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and amortization. Depreciation and amortization are computed generally on the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets. Upon the sale or other disposition of assets, the cost and related accumulated depreciation are retired and the resulting gain or loss is recognized. Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred, while renewals and improvements are capitalized. Software costs related to externally developed systems are capitalized at cost less accumulated amortization. Amortization is computed on the straight-line method over the estimated useful life<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">BANK OWNED LIFE INSURANCE</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Bank owned life insurance policies are stated at the current cash surrender value of the policy<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, or the policy death proceeds less any obligation to provide a death benefit to an insured&rsquo;s beneficiaries if that value is less than the cash surrender value. Increases in the asset value are recorded as earnings in other income.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">COMPREHENSIVE INCOME</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Accounting principles generally require that revenue, expenses, gains, and losses be included in net income. Certain changes in assets and liabilities, however, such as unrealized gains and losses on securities available for sale, <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">and amounts recognized related to postretirement benefit plans (gains and losses, prior service costs, and transition assets or obligations), are reported as a direct adjustment to the equity section of the balance sheet. Such items, along with net income, are components of comprehensive income.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The components of accumulated other comprehensive loss and related tax effects are as follows:</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">For the purpose of the consolidated statement of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents include cash and balances due from banks and federal funds sold with original maturities within <em data-td-fact-id="27588678" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">90</em> days.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">DEPOSIT LIABILITIES</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The estimated fair value of non-maturity deposit accounts, such as checking, savings, and money market demand deposit accounts, is represented by the amounts payable on demand. The estimated fair value of time deposits, such as <font style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">certificates of deposit and individual retirement accounts, is calculated by discounting the scheduled cash flows using the period-end rates offered on these instruments. As such, the Corporation classifies the estimated fair value of deposit liabilities as Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588679" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">INCOME TAXES</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined using the liability (or balance sheet) method. Under this method, the net deferred tax asset or liability is determined based on the tax effects of the various temporary differences between the book and tax bases of the various balance sheet assets and liabilities and gives current recognition to changes in tax rates and laws.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Corporation has several stock based compensation plans (Note <em data-td-fact-id="27588680" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">15</em>). <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The total amount of compensation is measured at the fair value of the awards when granted, and this cost is expensed over the required service period, which is normally the vesting period of the options. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">OFF BALANCE SHEET INSTRUMENTS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In the ordinary course of business, the Corporation has entered into commitments to extend credit, including commitments under credit card arrangements, home equity lines of credit, commercial letters of credit <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">and standby letters of credit. Such financial instruments are recorded when they are funded. Additional information regarding Off Balance Sheet Instruments is included in Note <em data-td-fact-id="27588681" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">17</em> in these Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">49</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">FAIR VALUE</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Corporation measures or monitors many of its assets and liabilities on a fair value basis. Fair value is used on a recurring basis for assets and liabilities that are elected to be accounted for under <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">the Fair Value Option as well as for certain assets and liabilities in which fair value is the primary basis of accounting. Examples of these include derivative instruments and available for sale securities. Additionally, fair value is used on a non-recurring basis to evaluate assets or liabilities for impairment or for disclosure purposes. Examples of these non-recurring uses of fair value include certain loans held for sale accounted for on a lower of cost or market basis. Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. Depending on the nature of the asset or liability, the Corporation uses various valuation techniques and assumptions when estimating fair value.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Corporation applied the following fair value hierarchy:</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588682" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> &ndash; inputs to the valuation methodology are quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets. The Corporation&rsquo;s mutual fund investments where quoted prices are available in an active market generally are classified within Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588683" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> of the fair value hierarchy.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588684" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2</em> &ndash; Inputs to the valuation methodology include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets and inputs that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instrument. The Corporation&rsquo;s borrowed funds and investments in U.S. government agency securities, government sponsored mortgage backed securities, and obligations of states and political subdivisions are generally classified in Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588685" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2</em> of the fair value hierarchy. Fair values for these instruments are estimated using pricing models, quoted prices of securities with similar characteristics, or discounted cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 36pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588686" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> &ndash; Inputs to the valuation methodology are unobservable and significant to the fair value measurement. Private equity investments and certain municipal debt obligations are classified within Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588687" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> of the fair value hierarchy. Fair values are initially valued based on transaction price and are adjusted to reflect exit values.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">When determining the fair value measurements for assets and liabilities required or permitted to be recorded at and/or marked to fair value, the Corporation considers the principal or most advantageous market in which it would transact and considers assumptions that market participants would use when pricing the asset or liability. When possible, the Corporation looks to active and observable markets to price identical assets or liabilities. When identical assets and liabilities are <em data-td-fact-id="27588688" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> traded in active markets, the Corporation looks to market observable data for similar assets or liabilities<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">. Nevertheless, certain assets and liabilities are <em data-td-fact-id="27588689" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> actively traded in observable markets and the Corporation must use alternative valuation techniques to derive a fair value measurement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">RECENT ACCOUNTING PRONOUNCEMENTS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em data-td-fact-id="27588690" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">No.</em> <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588691" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2014</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27588692" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">09,</em> Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27588693" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">606</em>). The ASU adopts a standardized approach for revenue recognition and was a joint effort with the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB). The new revenue recognition standard is based on a core principle of recognizing revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services. The ASU does <em data-td-fact-id="27588694" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> apply to financial instruments. The ASU is effective for public entities for annual reporting periods beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 15, 2017, </em>including interim periods within that period (therefore, for the year ending <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2018 </em>for the Corporation). Given that the ASU does <em data-td-fact-id="27588695" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> apply to financial instruments, which constitute a significant portion of our revenue, Management reviewed our non-interest sources of revenue and determined that the standard will <em data-td-fact-id="27588696" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> have a material effect on the Corporation&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> March 2017, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em data-td-fact-id="27588697" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588698" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27588699" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">08,</em> Receivables <font style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&ndash; Nonrefundable Fees and Other Costs (Subtopic <em data-td-fact-id="27588700" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">310</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27588701" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">20</em>). The ASU shortens the amortization period for certain purchased callable debt securities held at a premium to the earliest call date rather than maturity. The standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 15, 2018 </em>and must be adopted on a modified retrospective basis. Management has reviewed the investment portfolio and determined that the standard will <em data-td-fact-id="27588702" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> have a material effect on the Corporation&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> June 2016, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em data-td-fact-id="27588703" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588704" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27588705" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">13,</em> Financial Instruments - Credit Losses: Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments. The ASU includes increased disclosures and various changes to the accounting and measurement of financial assets including the Company<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s loans and available-for-sale and held-to-maturity debt securities. Each financial asset presented on the balance sheet would have a unique allowance for credit losses valuation account that is deducted from the amortized cost basis to present the net carrying value at the amount expected to be collected on the financial asset. The amendments in this ASU also eliminate the probable initial recognition threshold in current GAAP and instead, reflect an entity&rsquo;s current estimate of all expected credit losses using reasonable and supportable forecasts. The new credit loss guidance will be effective for the Company&#39;s year ending <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2020. </em>Upon adoption, the ASU will be applied using a modified retrospective transition method to the beginning of the <em data-td-fact-id="27588706" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">first</em> reporting period in which the guidance is effective. A prospective transition approach is required for debt securities for which an other-than-temporary impairment had been recognized before the effective date. Early adoption for all institutions is permitted for fiscal years beginning after <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 15, 2018, </em>including interim periods within those fiscal years. The standard will likely have a significant effect on the Company&#39;s consolidated financial statements as from a onetime adjustment to increase the ALLL upon adoption of the standard and due to increased provision expense at the time loans are originated.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> February 2018, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update (ASU) <em data-td-fact-id="27588707" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">No.</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588708" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2018</em>-<em data-td-fact-id="27588709" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">02,</em> Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic <em data-td-fact-id="27588710" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">220</em>): Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects from Accumulated <font style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Other Comprehensive Income. The ASU provides guidance on accounting for the effects of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, which was enacted in <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December, 2017. </em>The guidance allows the Corporation to reclassify the tax effects that were stranded in AOCI as a result of the tax rate change from AOCI to Retained Earnings. The guidance is required to be applied on a retrospective basis to all provisions of the ASU for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em>resulting in <em data-td-fact-id="27588711" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1,268,000</em> being reclassified from AOCI to retained earnings. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">50</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank is required by regulatory agencies to maintain legal reserve requirements based on the level of balances in deposit categories. Cash balances restricted from usage due to these requirements were <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588713" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$4,941,000</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588714" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$5,183,000</em> at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588715" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> respectively. <div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653146001" id="thunderdome-statement-801916">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman,Times,serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588719" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em>)<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Investment Securitie</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following is a summary of the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s investment securities portfolio as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588720" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em> (<em data-td-fact-id="27588721" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-taggable-table="table" data-td-v2v-id="1519653145990" id="thunderdome-statement-801917">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="finTable" id="null" style="margin: 0pt auto 0pt 18pt; width: 95%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">

		<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; vertical-align: bottom;">
			<td style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</td>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The investment securities portfolio is evaluated for impairment throughout the year. <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Impairment is recorded against individual securities, unless the decrease in fair value is attributable to interest rates or the lack of an active market, and management determines that the Company has the intent and ability to hold the investment for a period of time sufficient to allow for an anticipated recovery in the fair value. The fair values of investments with an amortized cost in excess of their fair values at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016 </em>are as follows (<em data-td-fact-id="27588723" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">amount of investment securities issued by government agencies, states, and political subdivisions with unrealized losses and the amount of unrealized losses on those investment securities are primarily the result of market interest rates and <em data-td-fact-id="27588724" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> the result of the credit quality of the issuers of the securities. The company has the ability and intent to hold these securities until recovery, which <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be until maturity. The fair value of these securities is expected to recover as the securities approach maturity. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016, </em>there were <em data-td-fact-id="27588725" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">205</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588726" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">230</em> securities in an unrealized loss position, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

In <em data-td-fact-id="27588757" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> new loans and other additions amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27588758" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$634,000,</em> and repayments and other reductions amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27588759" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$2,832,000.</em> In <em data-td-fact-id="27588760" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> new loans and other additions amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27588761" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$2,202,000,</em> and repayments and other reductions amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27588762" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$607,000.</em> In Management&rsquo;s judgment, these loans were made on substantially the same terms and conditions as those made to other borrowers, and do <em data-td-fact-id="27588763" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> represent more than the normal risk of collectibility or present other unfavorable features.</font></p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7678" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653170544" id="thunderdome-statement-801926">
<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588764" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5</em>)</b>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<b>Allowance For Loan Losses</b><b> and Credit Quality of Loans</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Company separates its loan portfolio into segments to perform the calculation and analysis of the allowance for loan losses. The <em data-td-fact-id="27588765" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">six</em> segments analyzed are Agriculture and Agricultural Real Estate, Commercial, Commercial Real Estate, Construction Real Estate, Residential Real Estate, and Consumer and Other. The Agriculture and Agricultural Real Estate segment includes all loans to finance agricultural production and all loans secured by agricultural real estate. This segment does <em data-td-fact-id="27588766" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> include loans to finance agriculture that are secured by residential real estate, which are included in the Residential Real Estate segment. The Commercial segment includes loans to finance commercial and industrial businesses that are <em data-td-fact-id="27588767" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> secured by real estate. The Commercial Real Estate segment includes loans secured by non-farm, non-residential real estate. The Construction Real Estate segment includes loans to finance construction and land development. This includes residential and commercial construction and land development. The Residential Real Estate segment includes all loans, other than construction loans, that are secured by single family and multi-family residential real estate properties. The Consumer and Other segment includes all loans <em data-td-fact-id="27588768" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> included in any other segment. These are primarily loans to consumers for household, family, and other personal expenditures, such as autos, boats, and recreational vehicles.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Each period the provision for loan losses in the statement <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">of operations results from the combination of an estimate by Management of loan losses that occurred during the current period and the ongoing adjustment of prior estimates of losses occurring in prior periods. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The provision for loan losses increases the allowance for loan losses, a valuation account which appears on the consolidated balance sheets. As the specific customer and amount of a loan loss is confirmed by gathering additional information, taking collateral in full or partial settlement of the loan, bankruptcy of the borrower, etc., the loan is charged off, reducing the allowance for loan losses. If, subsequent to a charge off, the Bank is able to collect additional amounts from the customer or sell collateral worth more than earlier estimated, a recovery is recorded.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">To serve as a basis for making this provision, the Bank maintains an extensive credit risk monitoring process that considers several factors including: current economic conditions affecting the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s customers, the payment performance of individual loans and pools of homogeneous loans, portfolio seasoning, changes in collateral values, and detailed reviews of specific loan relationships. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company utilizes an internal loan grading system to assign a risk grade to <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">commercial loans and each credit relationship with more than <em data-td-fact-id="27588772" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$250,000</em> of aggregate credit exposure. Grades <em data-td-fact-id="27588773" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">10</em> through <em data-td-fact-id="27588774" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">45</em> are considered &ldquo;pass&rdquo; credits and grades <em data-td-fact-id="27588775" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">50</em> through <em data-td-fact-id="27588776" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">90</em> are considered &ldquo;watch&rdquo; credits and are subject to greater scrutiny. Loans with grades <em data-td-fact-id="27588777" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">60</em> and higher are considered substandard and most are evaluated for impairment. A description of the general characteristics of each grade is as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The assessment of compensating factors <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>result in a rating plus or minus <em data-td-fact-id="27588815" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">one</em> grade from those listed above. These factors include, but are <em data-td-fact-id="27588816" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> limited to collateral, guarantors, environmental conditions, history, plan/projection reasonableness, quality of information, and payment delinquency.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Loans are considered past due when contractually required payment of interest or principal has <em data-td-fact-id="27588819" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> been received. The amount classified as past due is the entire principal balance outstanding of the loan, <em data-td-fact-id="27588820" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> just the amount of payments that are past due. The following is a summary of past due loans as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588821" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588822" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em> (<em data-td-fact-id="27588823" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Loans are placed on non-accrual status when, in the opinion of Management, the collection of additional interest is doubtful. Loans are automatically placed on non-accrual status upon becoming <em data-td-fact-id="27588824" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">ninety</em> days past due, however, loans <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be placed on non-accrual status regardless of whether or <em data-td-fact-id="27588825" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> they are past due. All cash received on non-accrual loans is applied to the principal balance. Loans are considered for return to accrual status on an individual basis when all principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and future payments are reasonably assured.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">For loans deemed to be impaired due to an expectation that all contractual payments will probably <em data-td-fact-id="27588829" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> be received, impairment is measured by comparing the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s recorded investment in the loan to the present value of expected cash flows discounted at the loan&rsquo;s effective interest rate, the fair value of the collateral, or the loan&rsquo;s observable market price.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following is a summary of impaired loans as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588830" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588831" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em>&nbsp;and <em data-td-fact-id="27588832" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015</em> (<em data-td-fact-id="27588833" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted):</font></p>

<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">61</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>agree to modify the terms of a loan in order to improve the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s ability to collect amounts due. These modifications <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>include reduction of the interest rate, extension of the loan term, or in some cases, reduction of the principal balance. Modifications that are performed due to the debtor&rsquo;s financial difficulties are considered Troubled Debt Restructurings (TDRs).</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Loans that <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">were classified as TDRs during the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016 </em>are as follows (<em data-td-fact-id="27588834" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted from dollar amounts):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">A modification of a loan constitutes a TDR when a borrower is experiencing financial difficulty and the modification constitutes a concession. The Corporation offers various types of concessions when modifying a loan, however, forgiveness of principal is rarely granted. Commercial loans modified in a TDR often involve temporary interest-only payments, term extensions, and converting revolving credit lines to term loans. Additional collateral, a co-borrower, or a guarantor <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be requested. Loans modified in a TDR are typically already on nonaccrual status and partial charge-offs have in some cases already been taken against the outstanding loan balance. As a result, loans modified in a TDR for the Corporation <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>have the financial effect of increasing the specific allowance associated with the loan. The allowance for impaired loans that have been modified in a TDR is measured based on the estimated fair value of the collateral, less any selling costs, if the loan is collateral dependent or on the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s effective interest rate. Management exercises significant judgment in developing these estimates.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The regulatory guidance requires loans to be accounted for as collateral-dependent loans when borrowers have filed Chapter <em data-td-fact-id="27588836" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">7</em> bankruptcy, the debt has been discharged and the borrower has <em data-td-fact-id="27588837" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> reaffirmed the debt, regardless of the delinquency status of the loan. The filing of bankruptcy by the borrower is evidence of financial difficulty and the discharge of the obligation by the bankruptcy court is deemed to be a concession granted to the borrower.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">At <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588838" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> the Corporation had <em data-td-fact-id="27588839" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> commitments to lend additional funds to the related debtors whose terms have been modified in a TDR.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588851" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">7</em>)&nbsp;&nbsp; </b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Deposits</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Interest expense on time certificates of deposit of $<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; <div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653197134" id="thunderdome-statement-801945">
<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(</b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27588872" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">8</em></b><b>)&nbsp;&nbsp; Federal Home Loan Bank Advances</b><b> and Repurchase Agreements</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank did <em data-td-fact-id="27588873" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> have any <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">advances outstanding from the Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588874" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank maintains an overdraft line of credit with the Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> The amount of credit outstanding was <em data-td-fact-id="27588875" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$0</em> as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588876" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em> The amount of credit available was <em data-td-fact-id="27588877" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$20,000,000</em> as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588878" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em> The interest rate on the line of credit is equal to the variable advance rate and is only charged on amounts advanced. The variable advance rate was <em data-td-fact-id="27588879" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1.67%</em> on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588880" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">0.90%</em> on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016. </em>The line of credit was subject to the provisions and conditions of the credit policy of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis. </font></p>
