<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588881" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> investment securities with a carrying value of <em data-td-fact-id="27588882" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$21,805,000</em> were pledged to secure the Federal Home Loan Bank line of credit. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016 </em>investment securities with a carrying value of <em data-td-fact-id="27588883" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$21,431,000</em> were pledged to secure the Federal Home Loan Bank line of credit.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> did <em data-td-fact-id="27588884" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> have any borrowings under Repurchase Agreements as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7682" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653208802" id="thunderdome-statement-802072">
<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(</b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27588885" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">9</em></b><b>) </b><b>Retirement Plans and Postr</b><b>etirement </b><b>Benefit </b><b>Plans</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-fact-id="27588886" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2000,</em> the Bank implemented a retirement plan that included both a money purchase pension plan, as well as a voluntary profit sharing <em data-td-fact-id="27588887" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan for all employees who meet certain age and length of service eligibility requirements. In <em data-td-fact-id="27588888" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2002,</em> the Bank amended its retirement plan to freeze the money purchase plan and retain the <em data-td-fact-id="27588889" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan. To ensure that the plan meets the Safe Harbor provisions of the applicable sections of the Internal Revenue Code, the Bank contributes an amount equal to <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588890" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">4%</em> of the employee&rsquo;s base salary to the <em data-td-fact-id="27588891" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan for all eligible employees who contribute at least <em data-td-fact-id="27588892" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5%</em> of their salary. In addition, an employee <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>contribute from <em data-td-fact-id="27588893" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> to <em data-td-fact-id="27588894" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">75</em> percent of his or her base salary, up to a maximum of <em data-td-fact-id="27588895" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$24,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27588896" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017.</em> In <em data-td-fact-id="27588897" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588898" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588899" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015,</em> the Bank made a matching contribution of <em data-td-fact-id="27588900" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">100%</em> on the <em data-td-fact-id="27588901" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">first</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588902" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3%</em> of employee deferrals and <em data-td-fact-id="27588903" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">50%</em> on the next <em data-td-fact-id="27588904" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2%</em> of deferrals. Depending on the Bank&rsquo;s profitability, an additional profit sharing contribution <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be made by the Bank to the <em data-td-fact-id="27588905" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">401</em>(k) plan. There were <em data-td-fact-id="27588906" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> profit sharing contributions in <em data-td-fact-id="27588907" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588908" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588909" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015.</em> The total retirement plan expense was <em data-td-fact-id="27588910" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$509,000,</em> for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27588911" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$512,000</em> for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016, </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588912" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$558,000</em> for the year ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2015.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank has a postretirement benefit plan that generally provides for the continuation of medical <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">premium payments for all employees hired before <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> January 1, 2007 </em>who retire from the Bank at age <em data-td-fact-id="27588913" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">55</em> or older, upon meeting certain length of service eligibility requirements. The Bank does <em data-td-fact-id="27588914" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> fund its postretirement benefit obligation. Rather, payments are made as costs are incurred by covered retirees. The amount of benefits paid under the postretirement benefit plan was <em data-td-fact-id="27588915" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$206,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27588916" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588917" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$205,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27588918" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588919" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$144,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27588920" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015.</em> The amount of insurance premium paid by the Bank for retirees is capped at <em data-td-fact-id="27588921" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">200%</em> of the cost of the premium as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 1992.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">A reconciliation of the accumulated postretirement benefit obligation (&ldquo;APBO&rdquo;) to the amounts recorded in the consolidated balance sheets in Interest Payable and Other Liabilities at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31 </em>is as follows (<em data-td-fact-id="27588922" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted):</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The APBO as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588923" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588924" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em> was calculated using an assumed discount rates of <em data-td-fact-id="27588925" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3.50%</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588926" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">4.25%,</em> respectively. Based on the provisions of the plan, the Bank&rsquo;s expense is capped at <em data-td-fact-id="27588927" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">200%</em> of the <em data-td-fact-id="27588928" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1992</em> expense, with all expenses above the cap incurred by the retiree. The expense reached the cap in <em data-td-fact-id="27588929" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2004,</em> and accordingly the impact of an increase in health care costs on the APBO was <em data-td-fact-id="27588930" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> calculated.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank Owned Life Insurance policies fund a Death Benefit Only (DBO) obligation that the Bank has with <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588931" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5</em> of its active directors, <em data-td-fact-id="27588932" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5</em> retired directors, <em data-td-fact-id="27588933" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">9</em> active executives, and <em data-td-fact-id="27588934" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">15</em> retired executives. The DBO plan, which replaced previous split dollar agreements, provides a taxable death benefit. The benefit for directors is grossed up to provide a net benefit to each director&rsquo;s beneficiaries based on that director&rsquo;s length of service on the board. The directors&rsquo; net death benefits are <em data-td-fact-id="27588935" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$500,000</em> for director service of less than <em data-td-fact-id="27588936" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> years, <em data-td-fact-id="27588937" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$600,000</em> for service up to <em data-td-fact-id="27588938" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5</em> years, <em data-td-fact-id="27588939" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$750,000</em> for service up to <em data-td-fact-id="27588940" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">10</em> years, and <em data-td-fact-id="27588941" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1,000,000</em> for director service of <em data-td-fact-id="27588942" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">10</em> years or more. The active directors who participate in the DBO plan have all waived the postretirement benefit. The executives&rsquo; beneficiaries will receive a grossed up benefit that will provide a net benefit equal to <em data-td-fact-id="27588943" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">two</em> times the executive&rsquo;s base salary if death occurs during employment and a postretirement benefit equal to the executive&rsquo;s final annual salary rate at the time of retirement if death occurs after retirement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7683" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653216727" id="thunderdome-statement-801953">
<p style="margin: 0pt 15.3pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588948" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27588949" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">0</em></b><b>) Stockholders&rsquo; Equity</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">During <em data-td-fact-id="27588950" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> the Company issued <em data-td-fact-id="27588951" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">129,962</em> shares of its <em data-td-fact-id="27588952" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> par value common stock to its Employee Stock Purchase Plan, for employee years of service awards, and for its directors<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo; deferred compensation plan. The aggregate value of these shares was <em data-td-fact-id="27588953" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1,447,000.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">During <em data-td-fact-id="27588954" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> the Company issued <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27588955" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">179,255</em> shares of its <em data-td-fact-id="27588956" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> par value common stock to its Employee Stock Purchase Plan, for employee years of service awards, and for its directors&rsquo; deferred compensation plan. The aggregate value of these shares was <em data-td-fact-id="27588957" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1,575,000.</em> During <em data-td-fact-id="27588958" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> the Company repurchased <em data-td-fact-id="27588959" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">192,080</em> shares of its <em data-td-fact-id="27588960" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> par value common stock for an aggregate value of <em data-td-fact-id="27588961" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1,414,000.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7684" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653227519" id="thunderdome-statement-801954">
<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588962" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27588963" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em></b><b>) Disclosures about Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Certain of the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s assets and liabilities are financial instruments that have fair values that differ from their carrying values in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. These fair values, along with the methods and assumptions used to estimate such fair values, are discussed below. The fair values of all financial instruments <em data-td-fact-id="27588964" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> discussed below are estimated to be equal to their carrying amounts as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27588965" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The carrying amounts of cash and cash equivalents approximate fair values.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">TIME DEPOSITS IN OTHER BANKS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Time Deposits in Other Banks consists of marketable certificates of deposit in other banks that were purchased as investments. <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value for the Bank&rsquo;s investment in time deposits in other banks was determined using the market value in active markets, where available. When <em data-td-fact-id="27588966" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are estimated using the fair value hierarchy. In the fair value hierarchy, Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588967" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2</em> fair values are determined using observable inputs other than Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588968" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> market prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets. Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588969" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> values are determined using unobservable inputs, such as discounted cash flow projections, for securities with <em data-td-fact-id="27588970" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> market activity.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">INVESTMENT SECURITIES</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value for the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s investment securities was determined using the market value in active markets, where available. When <em data-td-fact-id="27588971" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are estimated using the fair value hierarchy. In the fair value hierarchy, Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588972" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2</em> fair values are determined using observable inputs other than Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588973" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> market prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets. Level <em data-td-fact-id="27588974" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> values are determined using unobservable inputs, such as discounted cash flow projections, for securities with <em data-td-fact-id="27588975" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> market activity. These estimated market values are disclosed in Note <em data-td-fact-id="27588976" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> and the required fair value disclosures are in Note <em data-td-fact-id="27588977" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">19.</em> The carrying value of Federal Home Loan Bank of Indianapolis stock approximates fair value based on the redemption provisions of the issuer.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">LOANS<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> AND LOANS HELD FOR SALE</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Loans Held for Sale consists of fixed rate mortgage loans originated by the Bank. The fair value of Loans Held for Sale is the estimated value the Bank will receive upon sale of the loan. The fair value of all other loans is estimated by discounting the future cash flows associated with the loans, using the current rates at which similar loans would be made to borrowers with similar credit ratings and for the same remaining maturities.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">DEPOSIT<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> LIABILITIES</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The fair values for demand deposits are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e. the carrying amounts). The carrying amounts of variable rate certificates of deposit approximate their fair values at the reporting date. Fair values of fixed rate, <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">fixed maturity, certificates of deposit is estimated by discounting the related cash flows using the rates currently offered for deposits of similar remaining maturities. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">66</div>

<hr style="border: currentColor; border-image: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); page-break-after: always; background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">
<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">SECURITIES SOLD UNDER REPURCHASE AGREEMENTS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">estimated fair value of the Securities Sold under Repurchase Agreements is estimated by discounting the related cash flows using the rates currently available for similarly structured borrowings with similar maturities.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">ACCRUED INTEREST</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The carrying amounts of accrued interest approximate fair value.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">OFF-BALANCE-SHEET FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The fair values of commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit and financial guarantees written are estimated using the fees currently charged to engage into similar agreements. The fair values of these instruments are <em data-td-fact-id="27588978" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> significant.</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">
<div id="PGNUM" style="width: 100%; text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">67</div>

<div id="PGHDR" style="width: 100%; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653237351" id="thunderdome-statement-801957">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27588980" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">12</em>)&nbsp; Federal Income Taxes</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using the enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be reversed. The Corporation and the Bank file a consolidated <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">federal income tax return.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 21.6pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">current and deferred components of the provision for Federal income taxes were as follows (<em data-td-fact-id="27588981" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000s</em> omitted):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In accordance with ASC <em data-td-fact-id="27588982" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">740,</em> the Company is required to establish a <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">valuation allowance for deferred tax assets when it is &ldquo;more likely than <em data-td-fact-id="27588983" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not&rdquo;</em> that a portion or the entire deferred tax asset will <em data-td-fact-id="27588984" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> be realized. The evaluation requires significant judgment and extensive analysis of all available positive and negative evidence, the forecast of future income, applicable tax planning strategies, and assessments of current and future economic and business conditions. The Company did <em data-td-fact-id="27588985" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> maintain a valuation allowance on its deferred tax assets during the years ended <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27588986" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588987" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In the ordinary course of business, the Company enters into certain transactions that have tax consequences. From time to time, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) questions and/or challenges the tax positions taken by the Company with respect to those transactions. The Comp<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">any believes that its tax returns were filed based upon applicable statutes, regulations, and case law in effect at the time of the transactions. The IRS, an administrative authority of a court, if presented with the transactions could disagree with the Company&rsquo;s interpretation of the tax law.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In the <em data-td-fact-id="27588988" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">fourth</em> quarter of <em data-td-fact-id="27588989" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015</em> the<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> Company agreed to a settlement with the IRS for an audit of its tax returns filed for the <em data-td-fact-id="27588990" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2004,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588991" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2005,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588992" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2007,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588993" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2008,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27588994" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2009</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27588995" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2010</em> tax years. That settlement was approved by Congress&rsquo; Joint Committee on Taxation in <em data-td-fact-id="27588996" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em> The Company remitted the taxes and interest required by the settlement and the audit is closed.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 24.3pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of <em data-td-fact-id="27588998" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> lowered the corporate tax rate to <em data-td-fact-id="27588999" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">21</em> percent, repealed the corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT), and allows for a federal refund of any AMT credit carryforwards. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the <font style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Corporation reclassified <em data-td-fact-id="27589000" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$2,343,000</em> from deferred tax assets to other assets.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&nbsp;</b></p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7686" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653247985" id="thunderdome-statement-801961">
<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27589001" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27589002" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em></b><b>) Regulatory Capital Requirements</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Corporation and the Bank are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the Federal banking agencies. Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory (and possibly additional discretionary) actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the Corporation<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements. Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, the Corporation and the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance-sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices. The capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings, and other factors.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Corporation and the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the accompanying tables) of Total and Tier <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27589003" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> capital to risk weighted assets and of Tier <em data-td-fact-id="27589004" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> capital to average assets. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em data-td-fact-id="27589005" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2013,</em> the federal banking agencies issued revisions to the existing capital rules to incorporate certain changes to the Basel capital framework, including Basel III and other elements. The intent is to strengthen the d<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">efinition of regulatory capital, increase risk based capital requirements, and make selected changes to the calculation of risk weighted assets. Beginning <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> January 1, 2015, </em>banks transitioned to the new rules and reported results with the <em data-td-fact-id="27589006" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">first</em> Call Report of <em data-td-fact-id="27589007" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015.</em> As part of the new rules there are several provisions affecting the Company, such as implementation of a new common equity tier <em data-td-fact-id="27589008" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> ratio, the start of a capital conservation buffer, and increased prompt corrective action capital adequacy thresholds.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27589009" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27589010" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> the Bank&rsquo;s capital ratios exceeded the required minimums to be considered well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action. To be categorized as well capitalized, the Bank must maintain minimum Total risk based, Tier <em data-td-fact-id="27589011" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> risk based, and Tier <em data-td-fact-id="27589012" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> leverage ratios as set forth in the tables, as well as meeting other requirements specified by the federal banking regulators, including <em data-td-fact-id="27589013" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> being subject to any written agreement or order issued by the FDIC pursuant to section <em data-td-fact-id="27589014" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">8</em> of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank is considered to be &ldquo;Well Capitalized&rdquo; as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, </em><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27589015" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27589016" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and there are <em data-td-fact-id="27589017" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> conditions or events since <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>that Management believes have changed the Bank&rsquo;s category. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7688" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653275801" id="thunderdome-statement-801967">
<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27589027" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27589028" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5</em></b><b>) Stock-Based Compensation Plan</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The MBT Financial Corp. <em data-td-fact-id="27589029" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2008</em> Stock Incentive Plan was approved by shareholders at the <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> May 1, 2008 </em>Annual meeting of shareholders of MBT Financial Corp. This plan authorized the Board of Directors to grant equity incentive awards to key employees and non-employee directors.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> Such grants <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be made until <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> May 1, 2018 </em>for up to <em data-td-fact-id="27589030" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1,000,000</em> shares of the Corporation&rsquo;s common stock. At the <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> May 7, 2015 </em>Annual Meeting of Shareholders, this plan was amended to increase the number of shares available for awards to <em data-td-fact-id="27589031" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1,500,000.</em> The amount that <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be awarded to any <em data-td-fact-id="27589032" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">one</em> individual is limited to <em data-td-fact-id="27589033" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">100,000</em> shares in any <em data-td-fact-id="27589034" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">one</em> calendar year. As of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em>the number of shares available under the plan is <em data-td-fact-id="27589035" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">371,921.</em> </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Grants under the Stock Incentive Plan can be in the form of Stock Options, Stock Only Stock Appreciation Rights (SOSARs), Restricted Stock Awards, or Restricted Stock Unit Awards.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Stock Only Stock Appreciation Rights (SOSARs) <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&ndash; </font></i><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">On <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> February 23, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27589036" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">94,500</em> Stock Only Stock Appreciation Rights (SOSARs) were awarded to certain officers in accordance with the MBT Financial Corp. <em data-td-fact-id="27589037" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2008</em> Stock Incentive Plan. The SOSARs have a term of <em data-td-fact-id="27589038" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">10</em> years and vest in <em data-td-fact-id="27589039" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">three</em> equal annual installments beginning on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017. </em>SOSARs granted under the plan are structured as fixed grants with the exercise price equal to the market value of the underlying stock on the date of the grant, but providing for a cashless exercise. Upon exercise, the officers will generally receive common shares equal in value to the excess of the market value of the shares over the exercise price on the exercise date. The Stock Incentive Plan allows participants to cover their tax obligations by returning shares to the Company at the current fair market value at the time of exercise, which <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>result in a reduction in equity at the time of issuance.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The fair value of each <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">SOSAR grant is estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model with the following assumptions used for grants in <em data-td-fact-id="27589040" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27589041" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27589042" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015:</em> expected option lives of <em data-td-fact-id="27589043" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">seven</em> years for all three; expected volatility of <em data-td-fact-id="27589044" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">33.54</em> %, <em data-td-fact-id="27589045" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">41.21</em> %, and <em data-td-fact-id="27589046" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">56.42</em> %; risk-free interest rates of <em data-td-fact-id="27589047" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2.20</em> %, <em data-td-fact-id="27589048" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1.47</em> %, and <em data-td-fact-id="27589049" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1.79</em> %; and dividend yields of <em data-td-fact-id="27589050" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1.83</em> %, <em data-td-fact-id="27589051" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1.50</em> %, and <em data-td-fact-id="27589052" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1.30</em> %.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

SOSARs Exercisable at each year end excludes SOSARs that are vested but <em data-td-fact-id="27589053" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> in the money.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The total expense <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">recorded for the restricted stock awards was <em data-td-fact-id="27589066" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$69,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27589067" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017,</em> <em data-td-fact-id="27589068" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$50,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27589069" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27589070" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$37,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27589071" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2015.</em> The amount of unrecognized compensation cost related to the nonvested portion of restricted stock awards under the plan was <em data-td-fact-id="27589072" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$0</em> as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em><em data-td-fact-id="27589073" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$4,000</em> as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2016, </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27589074" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$13,000</em> as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2015.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Restricted stock units are valued based on the share price at the date of grant multiplied by the number of units granted<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">. The performance objective is expected to be met and <em data-td-fact-id="27589077" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">24,000</em> shares are expected to be awarded upon completion of the vesting period. The grant date value of the stock was <em data-td-fact-id="27589078" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$10.90</em> per share and the total value of the restricted stock units granted in <em data-td-fact-id="27589079" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> was <em data-td-fact-id="27589080" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$262,000.</em> </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Key executives were granted <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27589081" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">35,000</em> Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> February 25, 2016. </em>The RSUs will vest on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 15, 2018 </em>based on the Bank achieving the performance target of <em data-td-fact-id="27589082" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1.21</em> cumulative earnings per share in the <em data-td-fact-id="27589083" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">two</em> year performance period ending <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017. </em>One executive retired and did <em data-td-fact-id="27589084" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> meet the vesting requirement. As a result, <em data-td-fact-id="27589085" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">5,000</em> RSUs were forfeited. Restricted stock units are valued based on the share price at the date of the grant multiplied by the number of units granted. The performance objective was achieved, and as a result, <em data-td-fact-id="27589086" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">30,000</em> RSUs were earned and will be awarded upon completion of the vesting period. The grant date value of the stock was <em data-td-fact-id="27589087" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$8.26</em> per share and the total value of the restricted stock units granted in <em data-td-fact-id="27589088" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em> was <em data-td-fact-id="27589089" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$289,000.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Accordingly, the Company recorded expense<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">s of <em data-td-fact-id="27589090" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$237,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27589091" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27589092" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$186,000</em> in <em data-td-fact-id="27589093" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em> for the RSUs granted. The RSU expense is accrued ratably over the performance and vesting period. The total unrecognized compensation costs associated with non-vested restricted stock units was <em data-td-fact-id="27589094" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$257,000</em> as of <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017. </em>The Stock Incentive Plan allows participants to cover their tax obligations by returning shares to the Company at the current fair market value at the time of exercise, which <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>result in a reduction in equity at the time of issuance.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The RSU agreements grant the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors the right to adjust the reported earnings per share (eps) for extraordinary transactions which <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>affect eps in order to ensure the pay for performance <font style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">relationship. The enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 22, 2017 </em>is expected to affect the eps, and on <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> February 22, 2018, </em>the Compensation Committee approved adjusting the reported eps performance by adding <em data-td-fact-id="27589095" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$0.19</em> to the eps reported for <em data-td-fact-id="27589096" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> and subtracting <em data-td-fact-id="27589097" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$0.08</em> from the eps reported for <em data-td-fact-id="27589098" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2018</em> in determining the amount of RSUs to be vested under the RSUs awarded in <em data-td-fact-id="27589099" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016</em> and <em data-td-fact-id="27589100" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

			<td id=".trail.6" nowrap="true" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; border-bottom-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); border-bottom-width: 1px; border-bottom-style: solid;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td id=".lead.7" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; border-bottom-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); border-bottom-width: 1px; border-bottom-style: solid;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td id=".symb.7" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; border-bottom-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); border-bottom-width: 1px; border-bottom-style: solid;">$</td>

			<td id=".trail.7" nowrap="true" style="width: 1%; padding-bottom: 1px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt;">&nbsp;</td>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Under current regulations, the Bank is limited in the amount it <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>loan to the Corporation. Loans to the Corporation <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em><em data-td-fact-id="27589105" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> exceed <em data-td-fact-id="27589106" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">ten</em> percent of the Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s capital stock, surplus, and undivided profits plus the allowance for loan losses. Loans from the Bank to the Corporation are required to be collateralized. Accordingly, at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017, </em>Bank funds available for loans to the Corporation amounted to <em data-td-fact-id="27589107" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$14,649,000.</em> The Bank has <em data-td-fact-id="27589108" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> made any loans to the Corporation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Federal and state banking laws place certain restrictions on the amount of dividends a bank <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>make to its parent company. Michigan law limits the amount of dividends that the Bank can pay to the Corporation without regulatory approval to the amount of <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">net income then on hand. </font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7690" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653299947" id="thunderdome-statement-802081">
<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27589109" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em></b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em data-td-fact-id="27589110" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">7</em></b><b>) Financial Instruments with Off-Balance Sheet Risk</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank is a party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit. Those instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk in excess of the amount recognized in the consolidated balance sheets.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s exposure to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the financial instrument for commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit is represented by the contractual amount of those instruments. The Bank uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for its other lending activities.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<div data-thunderdome-xbrl-exclude="1" id="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-right: 0pt; margin-left: 0pt;">

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is <em data-td-fact-id="27589112" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> violation of any condition established in the contract. Most commercial lines of credit are secured by real estate mortgages or other collateral, generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses, and require payment of a fee. Since the lines of credit <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>expire without being drawn upon, the total committed amounts do <em data-td-fact-id="27589113" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements. Credit card lines of credit have various established expiration dates, but are fundable on demand. Home equity lines of credit are secured by real estate mortgages, a majority of which have <em data-td-fact-id="27589114" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">ten</em> year expiration dates, but are fundable on demand. The Bank evaluates each customer<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s creditworthiness on a case by case basis. The amount of the collateral obtained, if deemed necessary by the Bank upon extension of credit, is based on Management&rsquo;s credit evaluation of the counter party.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Standby letters of credit written are conditional commitments issued by the Bank to guarantee the performance of a customer to a <em data-td-fact-id="27589115" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">third</em> party. Those guarantees are primarily issued to support public and private borrowing arrangements and other business transactions.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> All of the <em data-td-fact-id="27589116" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">$1,364,000</em> of the standby letters of credit expire in <em data-td-fact-id="27589117" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2018.</em> The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved in extending loan facilities to customers.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Various legal claims also arise from time to time in the normal course of business, which, in the opinion of management, will have <em data-td-fact-id="27589118" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">no</em> material effect on the Company<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7691" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653311238" id="thunderdome-statement-801980">

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="7692" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1519653321700" id="thunderdome-statement-801983">
<p style="margin: 0pt 9.35pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em data-td-fact-id="27589122" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">19</em>) Fair Value Disclosures</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following tables present information about the Corporation<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27589123" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016,</em> and the valuation techniques used by the Corporation to determine those fair values.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In general, fair values determined by Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589124" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">1</em> inputs use quoted prices in active markets for identical assets that the <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Corporation has the ability to access.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Fair values determined by Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589125" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2</em> inputs use other inputs that are observable, either directly or indirectly. These Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589126" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2</em> inputs include quoted prices for similar assets in active markets, and other inputs such as interest rates and yield curves that are observable at commonly quoted intervals.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589127" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> inputs are unobservable inputs, including inputs that are available in situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the related asset.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> The Corporation did <em data-td-fact-id="27589128" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> utilize Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589129" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> inputs to measure the fair values of any assets on a recurring basis at <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> December 31, 2017 </em>and <em data-td-fact-id="27589130" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In instances where inputs used to measure fair value fall into different levels in the above fair value hierarchy, fair value measurements in their entirety are categorized based on the lowest level input that is significant to the valuation. The Co<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">rporation&rsquo;s assessment of the significance of particular inputs to these fair value measurements requires judgment and considers factors specific to each asset. Assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis are as follows (<em data-td-fact-id="27589131" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">000&rsquo;s</em> omitted):</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company did <em data-td-fact-id="27589132" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">not</em> purchase any Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589133" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> available for sale securities during <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><em data-td-fact-id="27589134" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2017</em> or <em data-td-fact-id="27589135" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">2016.</em></font></p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Both observable and unobservable inputs <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>be used to determine the fair value of positions classified as Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589136" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> assets. As a result, the unrealized gains and losses for these assets presented in the tables above <em data-td-invalid-detail="1" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;"> may </em>include changes in fair value that were attributable to both observable and unobservable inputs.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company also has assets that under certain conditions are subject to measurement at fair value on a non-recurring basis. These assets include held to maturity investments and loans. The Company estimated the fair values of these assets using Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589137" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> inputs, specifically discounted cash flow projections.</p>

<p style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 13.5pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Impaired loans categorized as Level <em data-td-fact-id="27589139" style="font-style: normal; font-weight: inherit;">3</em> assets consist of non-homogenous loans that are considered impaired. The Co<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">rporation estimates the fair value of the loans based on the present value of expected future cash flows using management&rsquo;s best estimate of key assumptions. These assumptions include future payment ability, timing of payment streams, and estimated realizable values of available collateral (typically based on outside appraisals). Other Real Estate Owned (OREO) consists of property received in full or partial satisfaction of a receivable. The Corporation utilizes outside appraisals to estimate the fair value of OREO properties.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 22.5pt 0pt 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Item </b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>9</b><b>. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">None</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Item </b><font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>9</b><b>A</b><b>. Controls and Procedures</b></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Conclusion Regarding the Effectiveness of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">MBT Financial Corp. carried out an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of its management, including its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of the <font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Corporation&rsquo;s disclosure controls and procedures as of December 31, 2017, pursuant to Exchange Act Rule 13a-15. Based upon that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that the Corporation&rsquo;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of December 31, 2017, in timely alerting them to material information relating to the Corporation (including its consolidated subsidiaries) required to be in the Corporation&rsquo;s periodic SEC filings.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Management<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The management of MBT Financial Corp. is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. MBT Financial Corp.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed under the supervision of the Corporation&rsquo;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of the Corporation&rsquo;s financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">MBT Financial Corp.<font style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&rsquo;s management assessed the effectiveness of the Corporation&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017 based on criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in &ldquo;Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013).&rdquo; Based on that assessment, management determined that, as of December 31, 2017, the Corporation&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting is effective, based on those criteria. The registered public accounting firm that audited the financial statements included in this annual report on Form 10-K has issued an attestation report on the Company&rsquo;s internal control over financial reporting which can be found under Item 8 of this form 10-K.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
